activity.title: Your smartest coworker has amnesia AI got smarter but somehow, I kept getting better at repeating myself Every new chat starts the same way: - here's who I am - here’s what I’m working on - here’s how I like things written - here’s the decision we already made Then I close the tab and do it all again tomorrow :( So, we built Cortex! Cortex gives AI a memory of your work it keeps useful context from your conversations, projects, and decisions then brings it back when you need it You can pick up where you left off Cortex already knows the work, the history & how you tend to think And yes, there are a lot of startups trying to solve for this issue and that's why we are open-sourcing Cortex Use it, pull it apart, improve it, or build something strange with it can't wait to see what you do with it :)) (link in comments! and my github)

i grew up in a small city in northeast india the kinda place where “one day i’m gonna work at a tech startup in silicon valley” isn’t a plan it’s a whole punchline, a childish dream somehow that punchline became uc berkeley and this summer, an engineering internship in SF! I’m happy to share i’m joining Magic Hour AI (YC W24) this summer. surrounded by people whose work genuinely stuns me and i get to build right next to them but i’ll be honest, because the clean version of this story isn’t the real one recruiting season, and freshman year took a lot out of me i showed up thinking the things i’d built back home the orgs, the products, the learnings would carry me here… but a lot of it just didn’t translate the things that made me stand out back home, were pretty ordinary in SF for a while i felt like i was just FAILING but i've since realised, that’s the beauty of this city SF (and Berkeley) with humble you in a 100 different ways you'll get rejected continously meet some of the smartest people and learn something new every damn day and in a way, thats the best thing that can happen to you SF keeps you hungry, keeps you wanting to build so if you’re in SF: coffee, shipping, or just a chat — my DMs are open

2025 changed my life in 100 ways Not exaggerating. Here’s why I have been MIA: 2025 started with a very chill version of me — figuring out life after high school while studying for my ISC 12th board exams. In January, I attended my high school farewell and applied to the top 5 unis in the world for a CS undergrad. I was completely set on taking a gap year, and building The Founderly in Bangalore. My mom convinced me to just “shoot my shot.” In February, I got into UC Berkeley MET. My life changed overnight. March was boards season. And for the first time in my life, marks didn’t feel like the center of my universe. From April to July, I maximised time with family and friends. Tiny trips. Long conversations. Silent realisations that everything was about to change. Then July took me to France to represent India at the ETEAM International Math Olympiad. In the first round, our team was second last. By the end, we finished second overall. (Thanks Lodha Group and Jane Street for this opportunity) That comeback still feels surreal. It was the first time I experienced how quickly things can turn when you refuse to give up. And then came August and September. The hardest months of my life. New university. New country. New systems. New everything. I was converting dollars to rupees in restaurants. Miles to kms in my head. Relearning how to communicate. Getting used to being misunderstood, and misunderstanding others. Back home, I was consistently at the top 10% of my grade. At Berkeley, I was surrounded by people just as driven, just as talented — if not more. I didn’t end with the GPA I was used to. Not even close. But I ended with perspective. I met some of the smartest and most inspiring people I know. My world became infinitely bigger, yet strangely smaller at the same time. Berkeley broke my confidence in a 1000 ways. But it also expanded my ambition in ways I didn’t even know were possible. Before coming here, I didn’t even know the kinds of things I could achieve. I didn’t know they were in the realm of possibility for someone like me. 2025 didn’t just change where I live. It changed how I see myself. And I’m just getting started. PS - I guess we are back on the Linkedin grind 🙌

How I got into UC Berkeley (MET, 2% acceptance) and Carnegie Mellon University (priority waitlist) as an International student from a Tier 3 city in India with no counselor and no paid programs Part 1: Testing & Exams Let’s be real — good grades won’t get you into top schools. They’re not a flex. They’re the bare minimum. Everyone applying to unis like Berkeley or CMU has 90%+ So yes, you need to have good grades — it’s kind of a mandate. there are many exams like SAT, APS, IELTS or TOEFL. Every college has its own requirements, so always double-check when u plan your exam dates. My SAT story — I was initially planning to take a gap year. which is why I didn't study before since i wasn't planning on applying to uni this cycle. But my mom convinced me to apply to my dream schools in the world. So that's what I did. 5 schools, No backups. I self-studied for a month and gave the SAT once in October. Somehow, I scored a 1510, with 780/800 in Math (which is what CS colleges usually care about). I didn’t take any APs — they were just too expensive for me. My academics weren’t extraordinary — just solid enough. With a grade CV, mid-level academics can be compensated for. Go to Part 2 to hear about my school grades, which were more important than the SATs. And if you have any questions, drop them in the comments :)) Follow my instagram for my raw insights on the whole process ;)

MET. i got in. it was one of the most surreal moments of my life — not just because it’s Berkeley, but because 14-year-old me, building websites after school, chasing wild ideas, and failing more times than i can count… never thought it’d lead here. and i was fortunately able to record my reaction on camera. Unfortunately, my high shrieking, crying, and laughing are too real for LinkedIn haha. so check this reel out on Instagram. no fluf, just the most raw version of me reacting to a life i can live. watch: https://lnkd.in/gx-d_AV2 that’s not just an acceptance letter, that’s a reply to a question i asked years ago without even realizing it. and for some moments, i was quiet (which is very unlike me). like, sometimes when a dream actually does come true, it doesn’t even feel like joy at first. it’s this stunned quiet, because the dream stopped being a dream for a second. it became real, and you almost don’t know what to do with it. like… “wait, this worked?” this one’s for every kid who built dreams off google docs, took risks that didn’t make sense, and believed in something before anyone else did. Every day when I open X or Linkedin, I see it Some founders just built an app in 3 days Another dude launched an AI tool and got 1,000 users overnight Someone else went from idea → revenue in a WEEK It’s wild. When I started Founderly in 2023, it took me FOREVER to build the damn thing I spent weeks tweaking fonts, picking colors, and making sure everything was perfect I wasted SO much time coding from scratch If I were starting over today? I’d launch in a week. Maybe less AI has changed the game You no longer need to be an engineer You don’t even need to hire a developer You don’t need years of coding experience With the right approach, AI can build your product for you The only question is: what are you gonna do with this opportunity?

I never thought that I would say this but I got into UC Berkeley! It was the most surreal experience ever, and in a way, it validated everything that I had been working on till now Previously, I had decided to take a gap year unless I got into one of the six schools I had applied to. All in the USA I can’t believe that I got into one of my dream schools, UC Berkeley I was admitted to the MET (Management, Entrepreneurship & Technology) program, one of the most prestigious dual-degree programs in the world, with only 50 students selected globally. I’m honored to be one of just two students from India in this cohort. Not only that, but Berkeley also sent me this awesome package (made me feel quite good 😋). The acceptance letter, a few brochures, a tote bag, a Mole skin notebook, pen, stickers and an MET cookie! It’s humbling to have made it through such a competitive process, and I’m grateful for everyone who’s been part of my journey. To my family, friends, and mentors—thank you for your constant support. And to the first few people who took a chance on a teen girl from Guwahati, hiring me for their projects—you believed in me before anyone else did. I wouldn’t be here without you. Now, on to the next challenge: finding scholarships! 😂

After securing second place at the ETEAM Olympiad 2025 in Lyon, Indian students Madhur Choudhary, Shresht Bhat, Anshveer Bindra, Adhiraj Anand, Vamika Singhal, and Vedansh Saha shared their reflections on the experience—from France’s academic environment to how it shaped their aspirations for the future. Their mentor, Mr. Sagar Shrivastava, Visiting Faculty at Ashoka University, spoke about their rigorous preparation and the importance of collaborative, research-based learning. With its globally respected institutions and strong culture of academic excellence, France continues to attract and support young talent in scientific fields. Initiatives like ETEAM reflect the growing strength of Indo-French collaboration, and the shared commitment to nurturing the next generation of innovators, researchers, and problem-solvers. For these young minds, France is more than a destination; it’s a launchpad. (Vijay) K VijayRaghavan Lodha Ashoka University French Embassy in India / Ambassade de France en Inde

Reforged Labs is winding down. We spent three years building AI creative tools for mobile game studios spending $500M+/yr on ads But it wasn't going to become the company we raised to build. The market is small. Our best customers signed six-figure contracts... but there aren't many studios at that scale. We tried expanding beyond gaming. It didn't work well enough. Then AI changed dramatically over the last few months. The models became so capable that we rewrote major parts of our own product around them. And I think our customers, some of the most sophisticated teams in gaming, will soon be able to build much of this themselves The gap we were selling into is closing. We could have kept Reforged going as a smaller business. The revenue was real. But I'd rather end it clearly than shrink it slowly. What I'll remember isn't the ending. It's a team split across the Vietnam & and the US ... shipping into some of the biggest studios in the world + a fraction of the people those studios have To that team: best people I've ever worked with. A few are still looking. If you're hiring in AI, my DMs are open Oscar Xing Luo and Lee Wang : building with you was the best part To our customers: you let a tiny startup into decisions where being wrong costs real money. Thank you for trusting us before it was obvious To Y Combinator , DCM Ventures , Epakon Capital , our many angels, and our supporters: thank you for taking the swing with us 🙏 I don't know what's next yet. For the first time in three years, I have space to sit with that question, and I'm not rushing the answer But I know I'll keep building 🚀

what the last 72 hours of building Kara (YC S26) looked like: > took a 5am flight to LA on my birthday for a chips conference > one of us flew back to SF for meetings > one of us flew to Baltimore for another conference > recorded our launch video > went on a podcast > received a fresh batch of diamond samples > we launched Kara internally to Y Combinator and are public - check us out: https://lnkd.in/g3XyzMpn > we spoke with hundreds of engineers, founders, and industry leaders 3 founders, 3 cities, and pretty much no sleep. the truth is building a company rarely is never as polished as the final announcement. It’s mostly airport terminals, conference floors, rushed calls and learning in real time. the biggest lesson: you cannot understand a market from behind a screen. Every conversation makes the opportunity clearer. grateful to everyone who took the time to speak with us. The diamond age is coming.
